newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Majority Leader sees budget progress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Majority Leader sees budget progress.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Sunday the Republican Congress would be able to work with the new White House chief of staff and that he believed progress would be made on the budget.

"I know we're going to be able to work with Erskine Bowles, he's a good choice and he's already been in contact with the leaders in the House and Senate. I think we'll make good progress," Lott said on ABC Television's "This Week."
President Clinton chose Bowles to replace Leon Panetta.

"He (Clinton) should submit a budget, we'll look at it, hopefully we won't have to say ... 'just trash it', hopefully we can say 'look, this is a positive first step, now let's work together on the rest of it'," Lott said.
He did not envision major changes in the welfare reform legislation passed in the last Congress.
"I do think it would be well-advised for us to at least let it go into effect and let's see how it works," Lott said.
